newsitem.title: UK: Arjo profits crumple, prospects may pick up.
newsitem.headline: Arjo profits crumple, prospects may pick up.

text.p: British paper and packaging group Arjo Wiggins Appleton Plc saw half-year profits crumple on Thursday and said although there was some pick-up in demand and profit margins, prospects for the second half remained fragile.
Arjo's first half pre-tax profits slid to 32.3 million pounds ($50.6 million) from 135.3 million pounds ($211 million) a year ago.

The company said in a statement the first half of 1996 and the second half of 1995 was "the worst period the group has experienced since its flotation," because of adverse market conditions. Arjo was spun off from B.A.T Industries in 1990.
Speaking of prospects for the second half, finance director Andrew Shaw said in an interview, "It is fragile, but there should be better volumes and a bit more stability in margins."
"There were weak volumes and pressure on margins" in the first half, Shaw said.
Pulp prices, the raw material for paper, collapsed from the end of 1995, after nearly two years of steady rises, dragging paper levels down with them, he said.

In Europe particularly, for carbonless and coated paper, margins were squeezed, he said, "but it looks as if that is over and that could make a big difference," he added. In the United States, the group's business "should see quite a pick-up," Shaw said.
